summary.headline: JTL Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43.0% YoY to INR 613.8 crores, with EBITDA per ton up 19% to INR 5,053 and volume up 23.2% to 1,00,484 tons.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 43.0% YoY to INR 613.8 crores, with EBITDA up 46.5% to INR 50.8 crores at an 8.3% margin and PAT of INR 29 crores (4.7% margin). H1 delivered record volume of 2,18,997 tons (up 20.2%) and record half-year EBITDA and PAT, though reported PAT includes a INR 2.78 crore non-cash depreciation charge from the JTL Defence asset revaluation. Management is pinning H2 on new GP/colour-coated capacity in Maharashtra, which depends on an electricity connection, and on export recovery after container shortages. Working capital days rose to 83 in Q2 from about 75 in Q1, which management attributed to material stuck on the floor during monsoon and festivals.

segments.name: JTL Industries (core steel pipes)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume of 1,00,484 tons with value-added products about 28,000 tons; value-added share of sales about 30-35% in H1. Exports about 12,000 tons in H1, with about 5,000 tons shipped so far in November.

segments.name: JTL Defence
segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 356 tons, with run rate about 140 tons in October, up from about 40 tons a month at launch. Management targets 250 tons a month by December and about 750 tons in Q4; capacity mandate is 1,000 tons a month, reached by FY29. Contributes about INR 200 per ton to EBITDA per ton.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target about 4,80,000 tons (about 30% growth on about 4 lakh tons in FY26). Base case H2 about 2,60,000 tons, which is 20% above H1; an analyst read the guidance as 5.15 lakh tons, which management did not confirm.
Exit run rate of about 65,000 tons a month by year-end, from about 40,000 tons a month today, once the GP line and colour-coated complex are running.
Exports expected at about 50,000-55,000 tons in FY27, with new trial orders in Canada and the US.
EBITDA per ton of about INR 5,000-5,250 targeted for FY28, with a similar level to FY27 because new capacity will ramp up slowly.
FY28 capacity utilisation target about 55% on 1.7 million tons capacity.
Value-added share of sales expected to rise from about 30-35% to about 50% in FY28.
Working capital cycle expected to fall to about 60 days by FY28 and about 35 days by FY29, as dealer sales rise and government sales fall (from about 20% to 3%).
Capex of INR 125-150 crores expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Maintenance capex of INR 40-50 crores in FY28, plus about INR 75 crores for the API pipe line, with the balance in H1 FY28.
capex_capacity: GP line at Mangaon (Maharashtra): cold trials of pickling and GP lines are done; commercial production expected by end of Q3 FY27 (December). Delay blamed on monsoon and material production; the line is awaiting an enhanced electricity connection. Expected to add about 10,000 tons once running, with about 25,000-30,000 tons expected from the new capacities in Q4.
Colour-coated/CRM complex: about 4 lakh tons capacity, expected to commission in December 2026; adds about 15,000 tons a month once it starts.
API line: now expected to commission by H1 FY28 (not Q1 FY28), serving both export and domestic markets, near Nhava Sheva port.
JTL Defence: entering coin blanks and bullet cups using existing raw materials; machines expected by end of FY27.
FY28 is expected to add new capacity to a total of 1.7 million tons, and management expects utilisation of about 55%.
demand_pricing: Secondary coil priced around INR 64,000 per ton, after an INR 600-750 increase in early November. HRC prices are high, but maintenance at Tata, SAIL and AM/NS is tightening supply.
Primary-secondary gap is INR 12-20 per kg depending on gauge (2.5 mm to 1.2 mm).
Demand latency ahead of Diwali; management expects demand to pick up after 15 November and a good H2 overall.
Exports hit by container non-availability and higher freight costs. The Strait of Hormuz disruption has affected the Gulf route for 6-8 months; management said the situation is dynamic.
Working capital days rose as material built up on the floor during monsoon, Ganpati and container delays. Management is exploring a vendor finance scheme with banks for dealers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GI/GP coil capacity (due August 2026) commissioned, and is the 4 lakh ton colour-coated capacity on track for December 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: GP capacity has cold trials complete and should start commercial production by end of Q3 FY27, delayed by monsoon and material production. Management expects 25,000-30,000 tons from the new capacities in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case H2 about 2,60,000 tons, 20% above H1 of about 2,20,000 tons, giving FY27 about 4,80,000 tons, which management said is on track for 30% growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the H2 step-up depends on Maharashtra capacity timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Start depends on the electricity connection, then about 15 days of setup. Management said the GP line could add about 10,000 tons, which could start within 15 days or as late as December; run rate could reach about 65,000 tons a month by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is targeted for FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55% utilisation in FY28 on 1.7 million tons, because new capacity comes on line.

qa_highlights.question: Will the API line focus on export or domestic markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is now expected by H1 FY28; it will serve both export and domestic markets, with the choice depending on which is more viable at the time.

qa_highlights.question: What are export volumes and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 12,000 tons exported in H1, with weak Q1 due to container shortages and freight costs. About 5,000 tons shipped in November; target 50,000-55,000 tons for FY27, with new trial orders from Canada and the US.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added product share, and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 value-added volume about 28,000 tons; share of sales about 30-35% to rise to about 50% in FY28. Working capital days expected at about 60 by FY28 and 35 by FY29, with government sales falling from about 20% to 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex in H1 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 70 crores spent in H1 by the company (vs INR 76.5 crores consolidated in the prepared remarks); INR 125-150 crores expected in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per ton is targeted for FY28-FY29, and what is the JTL Defence outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 EBITDA per ton of about INR 5,000-5,250. Defence adds about INR 200 per ton now and is expected to add more than INR 200 later. Defence run rate about 140 tons in October, targeting 250 tons in December and 750 tons in Q4, with 1,000 tons a month by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are maintenance and API capex needs for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex INR 40-50 crores in FY28 across Industries and Defence, plus about INR 75 crores for the API pipe line, with the remainder in H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand, and what is the primary-secondary spread?
qa_highlights.answer: Secondary coil around INR 64,000 per ton after a INR 600-750 hike. Primary-secondary gap INR 12-20 per kg; demand latency before Diwali, with a good H2 expected.

risks_watch: GP line at Mangaon depends on an enhanced electricity connection; start could slip to December, and H2 volume and the 65,000 tons/month exit rate rest on it.
Colour-coated/CRM complex (about 4 lakh tons) is due December 2026; any slip would push the 25,000-30,000 tons Q4 contribution and FY28 utilisation of about 55% on 1.7 million tons.
Exports depend on container availability and freight costs; management called the situation dynamic, and H2 export target of 50,000-55,000 tons needs Canada/US orders before Christmas.
Working capital cycle rose to 83 days in Q2 from about 75 in Q1; the targets of about 60 days in FY28 and 35 days in FY29 depend on a vendor finance scheme and falling government sales.
Analyst-implied FY27 guidance of 5.15 lakh tons versus the company's 4.8 lakh tons base case; management did not confirm the higher figure.
JTL Defence ramp to 250 tons/month by December and 750 tons in Q4 from about 140 tons in October, plus the API line now due by H1 FY28.
key_quotes: Our H2 is usually 20% higher than H1. So in a base case scenario, 2,60,000 tons something that you will see showing in H2
So it is very tough to say right now that what would be the scenario going forward.
So the INR 5,000 EBITDA per ton this year also includes about INR 200 EBITDA per ton being added from JTL Defence as well.
So we can expect that we'll be moving around EBITDA per ton of about INR 5,000 to about INR 5,250 for the next financial year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and demand, with H2 framed as a strong period. Cautious on timing: management repeatedly said the Maharashtra GP line and colour-coated capacity depend on the electricity connection and monsoon/material delays, and was non-committal on export container availability ("very tough to say right now").

adds.what: GP (galvanised plain) line at Mangaon, Maharashtra, ~10,000 tons once running
Colour-coated/CRM complex, ~4 lakh tons capacity, adds ~15,000 tons a month once started
API pipe line near Nhava Sheva port, export and domestic
JTL Defence coin blanks and bullet cups lines, machines expected by end of FY27

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume of about 4,80,000 tons (about 30% growth), with H2 needing about 2,60,000 tons, 20% above H1, backed by the Mangaon GP line (~10,000 tons, awaiting electricity connection, due December) and the 4 lakh ton colour-coated complex (due December); the H2 step-up depends on these lines starting on time.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY28 EBITDA per ton of INR 5,000-5,250, roughly flat on FY27 (H1 FY27 INR 5,000/ton), with value-added share rising from 30-35% to about 50% and Defence adding about INR 200/ton, so margin gains are guided but modest.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: GP line at Mangaon (~10,000 tons) targeted for December 2026 after cold trials, and the 4 lakh ton colour-coated/CRM complex due December 2026 adding ~15,000 tons a month, though both hinge on the electricity connection and could slip.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 base case ~4,80,000 tons (30% growth) needs H2 of ~2,60,000 tons, 20% above H1's 2,18,997, with exit run rate ~65,000 tons/month from ~40,000 today.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR 125-150 crores is firmly guided for Q3 and Q4 FY27, with utilisation around 40,000 tons/month run rate and FY28 capacity targeted at 1.7 million tons, so new spend is already committed rather than a fresh announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not confirm the analyst-implied 5.15 lakh ton FY27 read, sticking to the 4.8 lakh ton base case, and export and capacity timing remain uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The H2 step-up depends on the Mangaon electricity connection (could slip to December), colour-coated complex timing, and Gulf container/freight disruption, with exports needing 50,000-55,000 tons for FY27 against about 12,000 tons in H1 and 5,000 in November.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Colour-coated/CRM complex (Dec 2026), GP line (Dec 2026), JTL Defence coin blanks and bullet cups (machines by end FY27), and API pipe line (by H1 FY28, export and domestic) are all guided.

rows.label: Export recovery and new Canada/US trial orders
rows.why: Management targets 50,000-55,000 tons of exports in FY27 with new trial orders in Canada and the US, but ~12,000 tons shipped in H1 and ~5,000 in November, with container availability called 'very tough to say right now'.

rows.label: Working capital cycle to 60 days in FY28, 35 in FY29
rows.why: Cycle rose to 83 days in Q2 from about 75 in Q1; the target depends on a vendor finance scheme with banks and government sales falling from ~20% to 3%.

rows.label: JTL Defence ramp to 1,000 tons/month
rows.why: Run rate rose from ~40 tons/month at launch to ~140 in October, with a target of 250 tons/month by December and ~750 in Q4 FY27, against a 1,000 ton/month mandate by FY29.
